html:
The Woman, Life, Freedom protests swept Iran from September 2022 into 2023, after a young Kurdish woman, Mahsa Amini, died in the custody of the morality police, who had arrested her for wearing her headscarf improperly.

The slogan "Woman, Life, Freedom" came from the Kurdish women's movement. Women and girls led the protests, pulling off and burning their headscarves, cutting their hair in public and dancing in the streets. Schoolgirls, students, shopkeepers and workers joined, in cities across every province.

The protests became the largest challenge to the Islamic Republic since the 1979 revolution that brought Khomeini to power, and the compulsory hijab he imposed. Security forces shot into crowds and killed hundreds of protesters, by rights groups' counts, and arrested many thousands. Several young men were hanged after quick trials.

By spring 2023 the street protests had faded. But many women kept going out without headscarves, an everyday defiance the state struggled to stop. The jailed activist Narges Mohammadi won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2023. Compare the Constitutional Revolution of 1905.
sum: The Woman, Life, Freedom protests swept Iran from September 2022 into 2023, after a young Kurdish woman, Mahsa Amini, died in the custody of the morality police, who had arrested her for wearing her headscarf improperly.
